html:
The second, lasting founding of Buenos Aires on the Río de la Plata, by the Spanish captain Juan de Garay in 1580. He came down river from Asunción in Paraguay with a group of settlers, most of them born in the Americas.

A first settlement had been founded in 1536 by Pedro de Mendoza. Hunger and attacks by the local Querandí people forced the Spanish to abandon it in 1541, and the survivors moved up river to Asunción.

The new town grew slowly. Spain wanted the silver of Potosí to leave through Lima and the treasure fleets, so trade through Buenos Aires was restricted for most of two centuries. The port lived on smuggling instead, with Portuguese and later British and Dutch traders, and on hides from the wild cattle of the pampas. In 1776 it became capital of the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and later of Argentina.
